Selection probabilities of a decision rule

Source: R/SelectionOC.R
SelectionOC.Rd

Computes, from the results of SimSelection, the proportion of simulated trials in which a decision rule selects each cohort.

Usage

SelectionOC(
  results,
  statistic = c("br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "ntb_lower", "wr", "wo"),
  threshold = NULL,
  admissibility = TRUE
)

Arguments

results

Data frame returned by SimSelection.

statistic

One of "br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "ntb_lower", "wr" and "wo".

threshold

Numeric vector of thresholds.

admissibility

Logical: use the admissibility of the benefit-risk scores ("br_diff" and "br_ref" only).

Value

A data frame of class SelectionOC with columns statistic, threshold, group and p_select, with one row per threshold and cohort (in the order of results), and, for "br_diff" with admissibility, a row "(none)" for the trials in which no cohort is selected. See SelectionOC-methods for print() and plot().

Details

In each simulated trial, the cohorts other than the reference cohort whose statistic exceeds threshold are candidates, and the candidate with the largest statistic is selected; without a candidate, the reference cohort is selected. A cohort with a missing statistic (for example a win ratio when no pair is decided) is not a candidate. The statistics are

  • "br_diff": the difference of the benefit-risk scores against target values from that of the reference cohort. With admissibility = TRUE, a candidate must be admissible; when the reference cohort is not admissible, every admissible cohort is a candidate whatever the threshold, and no cohort is selected when none is admissible.

  • "br_ref": the benefit-risk score relative to the reference cohort. With admissibility = TRUE, a candidate must also be admissible relative to the reference cohort.

  • "ntb", "ntb_lower", "wr", "wo": the net treatment benefit against the reference cohort, its lower confidence bound, the win ratio and the win odds.

The default thresholds are 0 for the differences and the net treatment benefit and 1 for the win ratio and the win odds; "br_ref" has no default.

See also

SimSelection, CalibrateThreshold

Examples

res <- data.frame(sim = rep(1:4, each = 3),
                  group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 4),
                  is_reference = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), 4),
                  br_diff = c(NA, 0.2, 0.1, NA, -0.1, 0.05, NA, 0.3, 0.4, NA, 0, -0.2),
                  adm = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE,
                          FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
                  ntb = c(NA, 0.1, -0.1, NA, -0.2, 0.05, NA, 0.3, 0.1, NA, 0.02, 0.01))
SelectionOC(res, "br_diff", threshold = c(0, 0.1))
#> Probability that the rule selects each cohort
#> Statistic: br_diff (Difference of the benefit-risk scores from the reference)
#> 
#>  threshold    A   B C (none)
#>        0.0 0.25 0.5 0   0.25
#>        0.1 0.25 0.5 0   0.25
SelectionOC(res, "ntb")
#> Probability that the rule selects each cohort
#> Statistic: ntb (Net treatment benefit against the reference)
#> 
#>  threshold A    B    C
#>          0 0 0.75 0.25
